newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Four accused in Bangladesh share scam get bail.
newsitem.headline: Four accused in Bangladesh share scam get bail.

text.p: Four of the 36 dealers and company owners facing arrest for alleged manipulation of share prices in Bangladesh's stock market have surrendered to the High Court and obtained bail, police said on Friday.
They include Salman Rahman, deputy chairman and three other top executives of his Beximco group of companies, who were granted "ad-interim bail" until Monday.
They will have to appear at the court of Dhaka's chief metropolitan magistrate (CMM) after Monday or seek to extend the bail from the High Court, police told reporters.
The arrest warrants were issued on Wednesday night by the magistrate's court following cases filed against the 36 by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

The SEC filed the cases on the basis of an inquiry conducted by a four-member committee headed by Professor Amirul Islam Chowdhury. The inquiry's report alleged the dealers and company owners had been involved in "fraudulent activities" causing volatile movements in share prices and losses to investors.
Police on Friday said the were still seeking the 32 people who had not surrendered.
Beximco has described the charges against its owners and executives as "baseless, motivated, without fact and frivolous."
The Beximco group owns two of the eight companies cited in the committee's report: Shine Pukur Holdings Ltd and Beximco Pharmaceuticals Ltd.
The report said: "Shine Pukur has a paid up capital of 2.52 billion taka with 25.2 million shares of 100 taka each at par.
"The committee found that the book value per share was 103 taka while the market price per share was 73 taka on June 30, 1996. The highest market price per share was 754 taka on November 28, 1996."
About Beximco Pharmaceuticals, the report said: "The company's 29.5 million shares (of 10 taka each) had book value of 29 taka as per a DSE statement.
"The market price was 67 taka on June 30 last year and the highest price was 551 taka on November 16 in the same year."
